title: Add authentication rate limits and security regression suite
summary: Added PostgreSQL-backed fixed-window authentication rate limits for OAuth initiation, callback failures, session management and account-security actions using HMAC-protected IP/session keys; generic Retry-After responses; bounded auth metrics; hourly cleanup; a dedicated CI security command; and consolidated protocol, redaction, collision, fixation and concurrency regressions.

tests.command: RAILS_ENV=test ... bundle exec rails test test/domain/identity ... affected requests jobs and OAuth concurrency

tests.notes: 12 checks passed; 253 Ruby files and 25 ERB files clean; Brakeman 0 warnings; importmap and gem audits clean

tests.command: RAILS_ENV=test ... bundle exec rails db:migrate:redo:primary VERSION=20260904055000
tests.notes: Migration reverted and reapplied with all indexes and constraints
No whitespace errors or matching secret material

migrations: 20260904055000_create_authentication_rate_limit_buckets.rb creates one internal bigint table with unique and expiry indexes plus scope digest count and window constraints; no existing table rewrite
decisions: Used PostgreSQL atomic upserts so every web process shares one limit boundary
Double-HMACed canonical IP digests and opaque session IDs and never keyed on email provider subject or account existence
Count callback failures without clearing them on legitimate success; fixed-window expiry prevents permanent lockout
Kept logout available while rate limiting session revocation and all sensitive identity link/unlink paths
An initial regression exposed Rails query caching of INSERT RETURNING through find_by_sql; both counter reads and mutation are now explicitly uncached
Adjusted the concurrency harness to four pooled connections performing twelve operations so it loads the boundary without deadlocking the configured test pool
risks: Users behind one NAT share anonymous OAuth initiation and callback-failure limits; responses remain generic and Retry-After is bounded
Correct IP grouping depends on production trusted-proxy configuration for Rails remote_ip; invalid or spoof-conflicting input falls back to a shared unavailable-address digest
next_steps: Prompt 024 builds the organization and membership foundation
Production rollout must apply the new primary migration before serving updated application code
